newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West power prices steady to higher with gas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West power prices steady to higher with gas.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the U.S. West were steady to higher Monday, taking some lead from higher natural gas prices amid a limited surplus power offer from the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA), industry sources said.
Spot November gas prices in southern California for Nov 1 were up about $1 from October 1 to near $2.70 per million British thermal units.

Also, BPA said it was offering firm power delivered Tuesday during heavy load hours at $22.50, with power to the Northwest valued at $23.00 and the California-Oregon Border (COB)/Nevada Oregon Border (NOB) set at $24.50, all with a 200 megawatt limit.
Non-firm power for Tuesday was offered at $21.25, with the Northwest priced at $22.00 and COB/NOB at $23.50 with a 400 megawatt limit.
In the spot market, firm, peak COB power for Tuesday was said to have traded in the $21.50-24.50 range from a Monday delivery price near $21.00 late last week, the brokers and marketers said.
Off-peak next-day COB power was quoted at $19.00-20.00 from a range late last week of $17.00-18.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the sources said.
November COB was assessed in the $19.90-22.20 range, while December over-the-counter trade was said to have reached as high as $22.30 per MWh.
Tuesday Mid-Columbia power was discussed in the $19.00-22.00 range from near $21.00 last week.
Off-peak Mid-C was said to be trading near $16.50 per MWh.
November peak Mid-C was pegged at $20.35-20.95, the sources said.
Peak Palo Verde (PV) power for Tuesday delivery was assessed at $20.00-22.00 from a range of $19.25-20.00 late last week, while off-peak next day PV was assessed at $14.00-16.00 per MWh.
November PV was said to have been talked in the $20.50-20.75 range early Monday but eased with offers closer to $20.50 by the end of the day, the sources said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
